title: Ten QPACK static-table entries are truncated at the RFC's line wrap, and the --check that exists to prevent this re-derives the same wrong table
evidence: The committed table holds `{"accept", "application/dns-"}` (:60), `{"content-type", "text/html;"}` (:82), `{"strict-transport-security", "max-age=31536000;"}` (:87,:88), `{"content-security-policy", "script-src 'none';"}` (:115) — also indices 41,44,45,47,54. RFC 9204 Appendix A prints those cells wrapped ("Any line breaks that appear within field names or values are due to formatting"). The extractor matches only rows whose first column is a number (tests/vectors/extract_rfc9204_static_table.py:42,63-66), so it drops the continuation line; `python3 tests/vectors/extract_rfc9204_static_table.py <rfc9204.txt> --check` prints 'rfc9204 static table: committed entries match the RFC' and exits 0 on the defective table. wt_qpack_static_entry is what INDEXED_STATIC/LITERAL_NAME_REF_STATIC decode through (src/http3/qpack_field_section.c), so a peer's static index 52 decodes as `content-type: text/html;`.
expected: The ten values are the RFC's full cells: application/dns-message (30,44), public, max-age=31536000 (41), application/javascript (45), application/x-www-form-urlencoded (47), text/html; charset=utf-8 (52), text/plain;charset=utf-8 (54), max-age=31536000; includesubdomains (57), max-age=31536000; includesubdomains; preload (58), script-src 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none' (85).

title: The draft-16 :protocol token is defined as the HTTP/2 capsule token, and the 'legacy' constant is the same string, so webtransport-h3 can neither be sent nor accepted
evidence: session_request.h:38 `#define WT_WEBTRANSPORT_PROTOCOL_TOKEN "webtransport"` and session_request.h:45 `#define WT_WEBTRANSPORT_PROTOCOL_TOKEN_LEGACY "webtransport"` are byte-identical, so the OR at src/webtransport/session_request.c:108-109 is x||x. The code's own comment at session_request.c:103 says 'Draft-16 section 3.2 defines `webtransport-h3`'. Draft-ietf-webtrans-http3-16 3.2/9.1: ':protocol ... MUST be set to webtransport-h3'; 2.1.2 assigns 'webtransport' to WebTransport over HTTP/2. The client sends the wrong token (src/http3/driver.c:1252-1253); the Swift reference uses the correct one (Swift/Sources/WebTransportHTTP3Core/HTTP3Constants.swift:97).
expected: WT_WEBTRANSPORT_PROTOCOL_TOKEN is "webtransport-h3"; the pre-draft "webtransport" stays as the separate legacy constant the server also accepts.

title: The stream-table reclaim decrements the opened-stream counters, so a session reuses stream IDs and then fails to open streams at all
evidence: src/quic/stream.c:459-463 reclaims every complete stream when the 32-slot table is full and does `(*opened)--` per slot; src/quic/connection.c:2305 derives the next stream ID from exactly that counter (`index = wt_quic_stream_table_opened_by_us(...)`), under the comment at :2303-2304 'so it is never reused'. After the first reclaim the counter no longer names the next index: the next open rebuilds a live ID (table_open returns WT_ERR_STATE) or an ID that was already used and finished (RFC 9000 2.1: 'A QUIC endpoint MUST NOT reuse a stream ID'). wt_quic_stream_table_close has no caller in src/ or apps/, so the sweep runs on the 33rd open; grep -rn reclaim C99/tests is empty.
expected: opened_by_us_*/opened_by_peer_* are monotonic counters of IDs issued; reclaim may free used[i] and count but must not decrement them.

title: The reset_stream_at transport-parameter codepoint is wrong, so the extension draft-16 requires is never negotiated
evidence: transport_parameters.h:64 `#define WT_QUIC_TP_RESET_STREAM_AT ((uint64_t)0x17f7586d2cb570)`, advertised at src/quic/transport_parameters.c:472; Swift sends 0x17f7586d2cb571 (Swift/Sources/WebTransportQUICCore/QUICTransportParameters.swift:144). The normative reference draft-16 3.1 points to (draft-ietf-quic-reliable-stream-reset-09 3 and 8.1) registers reset_stream_at as 0x1d: 'Value: 0x1d, Parameter Name: reset_stream_at'. C99's non-empty-value check (transport_parameters.c:250-258) is likewise enforced on the wrong codepoint. The RESET_STREAM_AT frame type 0x24 is correct.
expected: The advertised identifier is 0x1d in both trees, so a draft-16 peer sees the extension both endpoints are required to send.

title: Two RFC 9000 18.2 MUSTs are missing from the transport-parameter value check: initial_max_streams above 2^60, and a client-sent stateless_reset_token
evidence: wt_quic_transport_parameters_check (transport_parameters.c:214-311) checks max_udp_payload_size, ack_delay_exponent, reset_stream_at, max_ack_delay, active_connection_id_limit, stateless_reset_token *length*, ODCID and source-CID lengths; `grep -n INITIAL_MAX_STREAMS` in it returns nothing, while the frame half is implemented (src/quic/frame.c:299,329). src/quic/connection.c:131-133 claims 'RFC 9000 section 18.2's own rules -- ... a stream limit above 2^60 -- are an error'. RFC 9000 4.6: a max_streams transport parameter above 2^60 means 'the connection MUST be closed immediately with a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR'.
expected: check refuses initial_max_streams_bidi/uni above UINT64_C(1)<<60 and a client-sent stateless_reset_token with WT_ERR_PROTOCOL and WT_QUIC_TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR plus the offender id.

title: A peer's initial_source_connection_id is adopted as the destination connection ID without ever being compared with the Source Connection ID of the packet it arrived in
evidence: connection.c:183-189 reads WT_QUIC_TP_INITIAL_SOURCE_CONNECTION_ID and calls adopt_peer_connection_id with it; the received packet's own SCID is decoded and stored (src/quic/packet_io.c:196-197) but never compared. RFC 9000 7.3: 'Endpoints MUST validate that received transport parameters match received connection ID values' and a mismatch 'MUST' be a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR or PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. The retry_source_connection_id half is checked (connection.c:216-226).
expected: The Source Connection ID of the first Initial/Handshake packet received from the peer is recorded and compared with initial_source_connection_id before the value is adopted.

title: A WebTransport unidirectional prefix split between the type and the session ID aborts the connection with INTERNAL_ERROR after the stream is already marked classified
evidence: driver.c:226-231 returns WT_ERR_TRUNCATED when the type varint filled the frame or the session ID varint is incomplete, but the call at driver.c:201 already recorded the stream as WEBTRANSPORT in the endpoint (src/http3/endpoint.c:473-477). deliver_to_handler (connection.c:1388-1405) closes with INTERNAL_ERROR on a non-OK handler status with no HTTP/3 code. On a retry, route_quic_frame sees a stored WEBTRANSPORT kind, sets finished_prefix=1 and passes the bytes straight to sink->on_stream_data (driver.c:687-694), skipping the session comparison at driver.c:238-241. tests/unit/test_http3_driver.c:79-129 only builds type+session ID in one buffer.
expected: The session ID is part of the prefix: the type bytes are held in the pending table until the whole prefix (type + session ID) validates, and the endpoint is told the kind only then.

title: Pseudo-header values are never checked for the field-content grammar, so :method/:scheme/:path/:authority/:protocol may carry CR, LF or NUL
evidence: The pseudo-header branch returns at headers.c:128 without calling field_value_is_valid; the grammar check runs only for regular fields (headers.c:141). RFC 9114 4.3.1/10.3 make a message carrying a character not permitted in a field value malformed. No in-tree echo was found that turns this into header injection (the CLI sanitises request_line at apps/support/session_loop.c:1141-1144), so the impact is a malformed, fully peer-controlled message accepted.
expected: field_value_is_valid(value, value_length) is applied to every pseudo-header value (and :method is required to be a token).

title: On Windows the monotonic clock wraps after about 21 days of uptime because ticks are multiplied by 10^6 before the division
evidence: time.c:35 `return ((uint64_t)counter.QuadPart * 1000000U) / frequency;` overflows uint64 once the tick count passes 2^64/10^6 ~ 1.84e13, i.e. about 21.4 days at the usual 10 MHz QueryPerformanceFrequency (minutes to hours where QPC reports the TSC frequency). After the wrap the value decreases, breaking the monotonicity the file's own header promises and mis-arming every QUIC deadline, idle timeout and PTO. The POSIX branch (time.c:24-27) is unaffected.
expected: Divide first: (counter / frequency) * 1000000 + ((counter % frequency) * 1000000) / frequency.

title: A peer's QPACK name length is narrowed with a bare (size_t) cast instead of the checked helper
evidence: qpack_field.c:56 `out->name = wt_cursor_bytes(c, (size_t)name_length);` and :58 `out->name_length = (size_t)name_length;` where name_length is a decoded varint (up to 2^62-1). The sibling string path guards explicitly (qpack_primitives.c:110 `if (length > (uint64_t)SIZE_MAX) return WT_ERR_LIMIT;`), and checked.h states the rule that a raw narrowing never appears in a length field. On 32-bit targets the truncation mis-parses the line.
expected: Refuse a name length that does not fit size_t (as wt_qpack_string_decode does) and use the narrowed value.

title: A stale frame-state pointer is written after the slot is released and refilled, desynchronising another stream's framing
evidence: driver.c:433 calls settle_capsule_stream, which goes to wt_http3_driver_forget_frame (driver.c:1146), which does `driver->frames[i] = driver->frames[frame_count-1]; frame_count--;` (driver.c:308-309). driver.c:434 (and the copy at :460) then writes `state->in_frame = 0` through the pointer into slot i, which now holds another live stream's state, clearing that stream's in-flight flag so its remaining payload is parsed as a new frame header. Trigger: a marked CONNECT stream's HEADERS completing while the frames table holds another stream mid-frame.
expected: state->in_frame = 0 is set before settle_capsule_stream, or forget_frame does not move the entry the caller still points at.

title: Capsules arriving in a later STREAM frame after WT_CLOSE_SESSION are still applied
evidence: session.c:144 checks only `wt_cursor_remaining(&ahead) > 0U` within the current cursor, and wt_webtransport_session_on_capsule_bytes never tests session state on entry (grep -n CLOSED src/webtransport/session.c finds only lines 27,56,62,66,79,92). The caller rebuilds a fresh cursor per delivery (apps/support/capsule_stream.c:76), so a peer can close the session in one frame and send WT_MAX_DATA/WT_MAX_STREAMS in the next, and observe still honours the grant. Draft-16 6 requires the stream be reset with H3_MESSAGE_ERROR.
expected: A delivery to a session already in WT_WEBTRANSPORT_SESSION_CLOSED is WT_ERR_PROTOCOL with WT_HTTP3_MESSAGE_ERROR.

title: A control frame whose loss re-send fails is never retransmitted and its descriptor slot leaks
evidence: connection.c:384-385 discards the status of send_encoded_frame, which frees the descriptor on failure (connection.c:766), while the control slot is deliberately left in_use (the only clears are the first-send failure at :708 and the ACK at :920). send_packet can fail with WT_ERR_LIMIT (congestion or sent-list full), WT_ERR_AGAIN, WT_ERR_STATE or I/O, after which no later loss names the frame: a MAX_STREAMS/MAX_DATA/NEW_CONNECTION_ID/RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID is dropped for the life of the connection and one of the eight control slots stays occupied.
expected: A failed re-send leaves the obligation outstanding so a later flush re-drives the retained control slot.

title: The suite is green on a retransmission assertion only because the synthetic clock stops 733 ms short of the earliest possible PTO, and the assertions pin behaviour the code has since fixed
evidence: The loop advances 1000 us for 600 rounds (test_runtime_session_pair.c:683,695 = 600 ms), while a connection with no RTT sample can only arm WT_QUIC_CONNECTION_INITIAL_PTO = 1333000 us (src/quic/connection.c:37,332-333). The retransmission the test says does not exist is implemented and wired: connection.c:3199-3227 hands the oldest outstanding descriptor to the lost handler on PTO, and apps/support/session_loop.c:377 resends the request. The test asserts 'the lost stream frame is NOT reported yet' and 'the exchange did NOT complete' (test_runtime_session_pair.c:756-758).
expected: The test advances past the initial PTO and asserts connect_arrived(&pair) != 0 (or records a known-fail), so it cannot pass because the clock ran out.

title: Always-true assertion: the 'unidirectional' property of every stream the endpoint opens is never checked
evidence: tests/unit/test_http3_driver.c:633 `WT_EXPECT_INT("streams this endpoint opens are unidirectional", 0, bidirectional ? 0 : 0);` evaluates to 0 == 0 for both values of the parameter.
expected: WT_EXPECT_INT(..., 0, bidirectional);

title: The two-pass writer property, the stated purpose of the helper used by all 26 frame round-trips, is checked by comparing a variable with itself
evidence: tests/unit/test_quic_frame.c:54 `(void)encode_ok(...)` discards the written length and :55-57 compares `wt_writer_offset(&measure)` with `wt_writer_offset(&measure)`. The helper's own comment (:36-38) says it 'Checks that the two passes agree, which is the property the whole writer design exists for'.
expected: Capture the return of encode_ok and compare it with the measurement, and initialise the decode cursor from it.

title: The synthetic clock is passed as the stream-id out-parameter and is clobbered to zero, so the loss scenario runs at time 0
evidence: tests/unit/test_quic_connection.c:1274 `uint64_t now = 101000000U;` and :1295 `wt_quic_connection_open_stream(&pair.client, 1, &now)` — the third parameter is uint64_t *out_stream_id and the callee writes 0 (src/quic/connection.c:2299). Every later send_stream(..., now) therefore uses 0.
expected: A separate `uint64_t id = 0U;` is passed as out_stream_id and `now` keeps the synthetic clock.

title: Two assertions in the malformed-input corpus cannot fail, including the only Retry check
evidence: tests/unit/test_quic_malformed.c:77 `WT_EXPECT_TRUE("a failed varint consumed nothing", c.offset <= length);` (a cursor can never pass its length; the property is c.offset == 0). At :162-168 the decode status is discarded and the assertion is `retry.total_len <= cut`, which holds on failure because the decoder memsets out (src/quic/packet.c:451) and on success because total_len == cut; the long/short-header blocks above gate on == WT_OK.
expected: `c.offset == 0U`, and the Retry assertion gated on `wt_quic_retry_packet_decode(...) == WT_OK` comparing total_len with cut.

title: An uninitialised endpoint is handed to the code under test, which reads its role and walks its request table
evidence: tests/unit/test_http3_driver.c:913 declares `wt_http3_endpoint_t other_endpoint;` with no init, :914 passes it to wt_http3_driver_init (which only stores the pointer), and :918 calls wt_http3_driver_on_quic_frame, which reaches stream_is_ours (driver.c:492-494) and wt_http3_endpoint_request_state, looping endpoint->request_count over requests[] (endpoint.c:299-306). Same pattern at test_http3_limits.c:117-119 and test_http3_malformed.c:245-246.
expected: wt_http3_endpoint_init(&other_endpoint, WT_HTTP3_ROLE_SERVER); before driver_init.

title: The peer-reachable field-name/field-value grammar fix has no regression test
evidence: src/http3/headers.c:136-144 records that a value of 'a\r\nX: y' and a name of 'bad name' used to pass, but every refusal in tests/unit/test_http3_headers.c:93-103 uses printable values (connection/close, transfer-encoding/chunked, keep-alive/timeout=5, upgrade/h2c, te/gzip) and the only invalid name is uppercase 'X-Test', which the pre-fix code already rejected.
expected: A refusal for a name carrying a space and for a value carrying CRLF (and a positive case for a space/tab value).

title: The container interop check cannot fail: the client's exit status is discarded and the script always exits 0
evidence: scripts/run-container-interop.sh:92-94 runs the client with `|| true`; a missing peer context only `continue`s (:66-69); there is no failure counter and the script ends with `echo "container interop: done (the client tool's own output above is the result)"` (:111).
expected: Drop `|| true`, capture the status, count failures and exit 1 when any session fails.

title: The compliance-matrix check never resolves the Evidence column, and 'the symbol exists' means 'the word appears somewhere'
evidence: scripts/check-matrix.sh:16 extracts only identifiers matching ^(wt_|WT_), dropping every test_* name the Evidence column is made of, while docs/COMPLIANCE-MATRIX.md:3-5 claims 'Every symbol named here is checked'. Lines 25-26 accept a match in any .h/.c file (comments and string literals included) or any CMakeLists/*.sh, so a deleted library symbol still passes if a test label contains the word.
expected: All backticked identifiers are extracted; test_* names resolve against the test CMakeLists/scripts and wt_/WT_ names against declarations.

title: The Definition-of-Done result is a hardcoded echo, and a requirement counts as 'exercised by a test' because its status cell says so
evidence: scripts/score-matrix.sh:40 `echo "definition of done: 8 of 9 criteria met, 1 partial, 0 not met"` computes nothing (the script's header and README.md claim the number is measured), and the 34/34 count at :38 is derived from the status cell alone — no test name is resolved or checked (see F-18).
expected: The nine criteria live in a machine-readable table and are counted, or the line is labelled as quoted prose.

title: Two hard CI checks exit 0 when the tool they need is missing, so green does not mean they ran
evidence: scripts/check-vectors.sh:43-46 prints 'unsupported' and `exit 0` when python3 is absent; scripts/check-static-analysis.sh:29-32 and :37-40 do the same when clang has no --analyze or python3 is absent. These are the evidence for two claimed Definition-of-Done criteria, and FreeBSD (a platform the docs claim passes the suite) has no python3 in its base system (docs/PORTABILITY.md:190-193).
expected: The guards exit with CTest's skip code 77 (or a non-zero status), so the aggregate shows the check did not run.

title: Documented counts contradict each other and no script produces either number
evidence: README.md:61 says '84 test programs and 91,552 checks' and README.md:290,293 say '72 library sources and 92 test/app sources' and '84 PE32+ executables'; docs/PORTABILITY.md:126 says '85 test executables ... the reported checks sum to 91,674' and :93,:103 say 76/108 sources and 91 executables. The tree is 76 src/*.c and 91 linked executables, and `grep -n checks scripts/check-windows-wine.sh` finds nothing — the runner reports no check total.
expected: One number per fact, produced by the script that measures it (76/108/91, 91,674), or no restatement.

title: 'the same warnings the POSIX build turns into errors' is seven flags, not the project's twenty-four
evidence: docs/PORTABILITY.md:76-77 claims the Windows sweep uses the same warning set; scripts/check-windows-platform.sh:36 uses -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Wshadow -Wcast-qual, while cmake/WTCompilerWarnings.cmake:23-48 adds -Wpedantic, -Wcast-align, -Wstrict-prototypes, -Wmissing-prototypes, -Wmissing-declarations, -Wold-style-definition, -Wredundant-decls, -Wundef, -Wwrite-strings, -Wpointer-arith, -Wfloat-equal, -Wswitch-enum, -Wvla, -Wformat=2, -Wnull-dereference and -Wdouble-promotion.
expected: The four command lines in that script carry the full project warning set, or the document states the subset.

title: A 'tested' draft-16 row claims strict increase for WT_MAX_STREAM_DATA, which the session layer deliberately refuses as prohibited
evidence: docs/COMPLIANCE-MATRIX.md:35 marks 'WT_MAX_DATA / WT_MAX_STREAM_DATA / WT_MAX_STREAMS strictly increase' as tested with evidence wt_webtransport_flow_on_max_data/_on_max_streams and test_webtransport_flow, but src/api/session.c:136-143 refuses WT_MAX_STREAM_DATA/WT_STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED as prohibited by draft-16 5.4 with WT_ERR_PROTOCOL, no ..._on_max_stream_data handler exists, and the test only round-trips the codec.
expected: The row is split: MAX_DATA/MAX_STREAMS tested, WT_MAX_STREAM_DATA recorded as prohibited by 5.4.

title: A no-op statement in the literal-literal-name encoder
evidence: qpack_field.c:105 `if (line->never_indexed != 0) flags |= 0x00U;` follows :104 `if (line->never_indexed) flags |= 0x10U;` and changes nothing; it reads like a missing bit.
expected: Delete line 105.

title: The harness reports a test file that ran zero checks as passing
evidence: tests/wt_test.h:116-125 prints 'all %d checks passed' and returns 0 when wt_test_checks == 0, with no floor. Related literal tautologies that inflate the count: test_quic_pn_space.c:211, test_quic_protection.c:252, test_quic_varint.c:200, test_tls13_keyschedule.c:493, test_webtransport_capsule.c:28, test_public_api.c:96.
expected: WT_TEST_MAIN_END fails when wt_test_checks == 0.

title: The 'inventory completeness' check is a fixed nine-name list, so it cannot catch a new POSIX call
evidence: scripts/check-portability.sh:15 lists fcntl poll recvmsg sendmsg inet_pton recvfrom sendto close O_NONBLOCK, while the library also uses inet_ntop (src/runtime/udp_platform.h:430,637), setsockopt (:312,510), getsockopt (:183), socket (src/runtime/udp.c:96) and bind (udp.c:145), none of which can ever fail the check — although docs/PORTABILITY.md:6,70 claims the inventory is complete and mechanically checked.
expected: The list covers every platform-adapted call (or is derived from src/runtime/udp_platform.h).

title: The diagnostics document describes a library-side secret dump the code says was deliberately removed
evidence: docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md:15 names src/tls/session.c as a WT_TLS_SECRET_LOG writer; src/tls/session.c:601-602 says that diagnostic 'is GONE', and `grep -rn WT_TLS_SECRET_LOG C99/src` returns only that comment. The live writer is apps/support/session_loop.c:608.
expected: The table names only the app, and the getenv cost paragraph drops 'a secret derivation'.

title: wt_http3_endpoint_write_prefix returns WT_OK without checking that the prefix was written, and latches before the write
evidence: endpoint.c:319-320 writes the prefix and returns WT_OK without consulting wt_writer_ok(w); the once-only flags are set before the write (endpoint.c:330,334,338). With a writer too small for the type prefix the function reports success, a retry is WT_ERR_STATE, and wt_http3_driver_start_qpack_stream propagates WT_OK while the caller sends wt_writer_offset(&w) == 0 bytes as the stream.
expected: return wt_writer_ok(w) ? WT_OK : WT_ERR_LIMIT; and set the latch only after a successful write.

title: wt_alloc_array reports WT_OK while returning NULL on allocation failure
evidence: allocator.c:82-83 sets `*out_status = WT_OK` and returns wt_alloc(a, total) without testing for NULL, where the sibling wt_calloc_array sets WT_ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (allocator.c:96-100). No in-tree caller (grep -rn wt_alloc_array C99/src C99/apps finds the definition only), so the impact is a public API that lies to its caller.
expected: Set WT_ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY when the block is NULL.

title: wt_webtransport_close_session_parse writes its out-parameter before a check that fails
evidence: capsule.c:144-147 writes *out_error_code, then :150 runs the UTF-8 validation and :152 returns WT_ERR_PROTOCOL, so a caller that reads the code after the failure reads a value from the capsule that was just refused, contrary to the out-parameter rule in include/webtransport/status.h.
expected: Assign *out_error_code only after the UTF-8 check has passed.

title: Three provably unreachable blocks in the driver and the API flow layer
evidence: driver.c:398-404 copies a header remainder that is always zero (the header loop breaks as soon as both varints parse, so leftover == 0); driver.c:723-730 tests kind == UNKNOWN after :708-711 already returned and no stored kind is ever UNKNOWN (endpoint.c:463-466); api/flow.c:149-155 handles flow_enabled != 0 && max_data_set == 0, which cannot occur because the only writer of flow_enabled (flow.c:43) is immediately followed by wt_webtransport_flow_on_max_data, which sets max_data_set = 1.
expected: The three blocks are deleted (or replaced by an assertion).
